narrative:
The model estimated a 76.6% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. Because that risk was high, your law school application was denied. This is a statistical forecast, not a final judgment about your ability.

The strongest reason was your third-year academic standing: your decile of 1 is far below the average of about 5.8 among accepted students, and it was the single most influential factor pushing the prediction toward failure. Your first-year decile of 2, also well below the accepted average of 6, was the second-strongest factor and likewise pushed toward failure. Your LSAT score of 29.5, below the accepted average of 37.2, was the third-most influential feature; in this case its influence leaned toward passing, but it was not enough to offset the two academic-standing signals. Your gender and race were not used in the prediction.

To proceed, ask admissions whether an appeal or reconsideration process exists and what evidence would help. Address the academic record directly: seek advising, consider additional coursework or a post-baccalaureate program, and provide context for lower early grades. If feasible, retake the LSAT after structured preparation. Consider applying in a later cycle or to schools with more flexible review, and ask for feedback so your next application can show a clearer upward trajectory and readiness for bar study.
